Surah al-Haqqah (The Inevitable Reality), Meccan, and its verses are fifty-two.

﴿The Inevitable Reality﴾: the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah), in which what was denied of the Resurrection, the Reckoning and the Recompense becomes manifest (yahuqqu), or the one that makes that manifest.
﴿What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ An exaltation of its status. It is a *mubtada'* (grammatical subject), and *al-Ḥāqqah* (the Inevitable Reality) is its *khabar* (grammatical predicate).

﴿And what will make you know what the Inevitable Reality is?﴾ That is, what informed you of what al-Haqqah is. The repetition is an increase in magnifying its importance. Thus the first *mā* is the *mubtada'* (subject of the nominal sentence), and what follows it is its *khabar* (predicate). The second *mā* and its predicate are in the position of the second object (*maf'ūl thānī*) of *adrā* (أَدْرى), which is the verb "to make know."
Thamud and ʿAd denied the Striking (al-Qari'ah) (﴿Thamud and ʿAd denied the Striking﴾), i.e., the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah), so named because it strikes the hearts with its terrors.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 5:

﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overwhelming blast﴾ — by the cry (al-sayha) that exceeded its limit in severity.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 6:

﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a furious, roaring wind﴾ (strong, violent, and harsh upon 'Ad, despite their own strength and might)

﴿Sakhkharahā﴾ (He subjected it) — sent it upon them with overpowering force. ﴿Upon them for seven nights and eight days﴾ — its beginning was from the morning of Wednesday, eight days remaining of Shawwal, and it was in the last part of winter. ﴿Continuously﴾ — uninterrupted, successive; it is likened to the successive action of the cauterizer (al-hasim) in repeatedly applying the cautery to a disease, one time after another, until the disease is completely eradicated. ﴿So you see the people therein laid low﴾ — cast down and destroyed. ﴿As if they were the trunks﴾ — roots — ﴿of hollow palm trees﴾ — fallen and empty.
﴿So do you see any remnant of them?﴾ You do not see any remnant of them.

﴿And Pharaoh came, and those before him﴾: his followers. In one recitation variant (qirāʾa, a canonical reading of the Qur'an), "qabalahu" is read with a fatḥa on the qāf and a sukūn on the bāʾ, meaning those who preceded him of the disbelieving nations. ﴿And the overturned cities﴾: that is, their inhabitants, and these were the towns of the people of Lūṭ (Lot). ﴿With the sin﴾: with the sinful deeds that carried error.
﴿So they disobeyed the messenger of their Lord﴾ — i.e., Lut and others besides him — ﴿so He seized them with a severe seizing﴾ — exceeding in harshness other seizings.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 11:

﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed﴾ it rose above everything, including the mountains and other things, at the time of the Flood. ﴿We carried you﴾ meaning your forefathers, since you were in their loins, ﴿in the sailing ship﴾ the ship which Noah built, and he and those who were with him in it were saved, while the others drowned.

﴿لِنَجْعَلها﴾ i.e., this deed, which is the saving of the believers and the destruction of the disbelievers, ﴿لَكُمْ تَذْكِرَة﴾ [as] an admonition, ﴿وتَعِيها﴾ and so that it may be preserved, ﴿أُذُن واعِيَة﴾ [meaning] an ear that retains what it hears.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 13:

﴿Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast﴾ for the separation among the creatures, and it is the second blast.

[Tafsir al-Jalalayn on 69:14]

﴿And the earth and the mountains were lifted﴾ — raised up — ﴿and they were crushed with one blow﴾ — they were pounded.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 15:

﴿So on that Day the Inevitable Event will occur﴾ The Resurrection will take place.
﴿And the heaven will be split open, for it that Day will be frail﴾ weak.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 17:

﴿And the angels﴾, meaning: the angels, ﴿will be upon its edges﴾, the sides of the sky. ﴿And eight will bear above them the Throne of your Lord﴾, i.e., above the aforementioned angels, ﴿on that Day﴾, eight [of the angels] or [eight rows] of their ranks.
﴿On that Day you will be exposed﴾ for reckoning, ﴿not a thing of yours will be hidden﴾ (read with both the taa' and the yaa'), ﴿from you, concealed﴾ from among the inner secrets.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 19:**

﴿Then as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say﴾, addressing his companions, out of joy at it, ﴿"Here, take and read my record!"﴾ (hā'um: take; iqra'ū: read). The verb "hā'um" and the verb "iqra'ū" are in dispute (tanāzu'): both govern the object "kitābiya" (my record).

The commentary text: "﴿إنِّي ظَنَنْت﴾ تَيَقَّنْت"

Translation:

﴿Indeed, I was certain﴾ I was certain (tayaqqantu)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 21:

﴿So he will be in a pleasing life﴾ [one that is] pleasing (marḍiyya)
Qutufuhā (﴿قُطُوفها﴾): its fruits. Dāniyah (﴿دانِيَة﴾): near, within reach, so that one standing, sitting, or reclining can pick from it.

Then it will be said to them, ﴿Eat and drink with satisfaction﴾ (hani'an), a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), meaning enjoying it without hardship, ﴿for what you advanced in the days that have passed﴾ (al-khāliyah), i.e., the past days in the world.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 25:

﴿And as for one who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: "Oh"﴾ *Ya* (يا) is for alerting (*lil-tanbih*).
﴿O, would that it had been the end!﴾ That is, the death in the world ﴿had been the decisive one﴾, the one that cut off my life, so that I would not be resurrected.

﴿My authority has perished from me.﴾ (That is,) my power and my proof. The ha' (ه) in كِتابِيَهْ (kitabiyah), حِسابِيَهْ (hisabiyah), مالِيَهْ (maliyah) and سُلْطانِيَهْ (sultaniyah) is for pausal ha' (al-sakt), and it is retained both in pause and in continuous recitation, following the standard codex (al-Mushaf al-Imam) and the transmitted reading. Among them are those who omit it in continuous recitation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 30:

﴿Seize him﴾ is an address to the guardians of Hell. ﴿Then shackle him﴾ gather his hands to his neck in the shackle.

ثُمَّ الجَحِيم — "Then into the Blazing Fire (al-Jahim)": the burning Fire. صَلُّوهُ — "Burn him" (i.e., "cast him in"): enter him.

Wait, I need to correct that: the tafsir gloss says أدْخِلُوهُ, which means "Admit him" / "Cause him to enter."

Here is the faithful translation:

﴿Then the Blazing Fire﴾ the burning Fire. ﴿Burn him﴾ cause him to enter.

Then, into a chain whose length is seventy cubits (with the cubit of the angel), ﴿then thread him﴾ (i.e., insert him into it) after inserting him into the Fire. The particle "fa" (then/so) does not prevent the verb from being connected to the earlier-mentioned adverbial phrase.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 35:

﴿So there is no close friend for him today here﴾ — a close friend (ḥamīm) who would benefit him.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 36:

﴿Nor any food except from ghislin﴾ (the pus of the people of the Fire), or a tree in it.
﴿Nothing will eat it except the sinners﴾, the disbelievers.
The particle ﴿فَلا﴾ is redundant (زائدة, *zā'idah*, an extra particle that adds no meaning): ﴿I swear by what you see﴾, that is, of the created things.
﴿And what you do not see﴾ of them, i.e., of every created thing.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 40:

﴿Indeed it﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is the word of a noble Messenger﴾, i.e., he conveyed it as a message from Allah, exalted is He.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Nor is it the word of a soothsayer; little do you remember.﴾ (ﷺ)

Note: the tafsir text here is a separate passage; translating it faithfully:

"With the ta' (تاء) and the ya' (ياء) in the two verbs (i.e., the verbs ﴿تَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ may be read with either the ta' or the ya'), and the ma (ما) is extra (mazīdah) for emphasis (mu'akkidah). The meaning is that they believe in few things and remember them, from what the Prophet (ﷺ) brought of good, ties of kinship, and chastity, so these did not avail them anything."
Rather, it is ﴿a revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 44:

﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings﴾ — i.e., the Prophet — ﴿some sayings﴾ — by saying about Us what We did not say.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 45:

﴿Surely We would have seized⦆ ﴿him⦆ ﴿by the right hand⦆ — by might and power.

Note on the passage: the bracketed glosses in the Arabic are the commentators' explanations of the verse's words. "لِنَلِنا" means "to take hold of him" (that is, the verb ﴿لَأَخَذْنا﴾ is explained as "لِنَلِنا," meaning "so that We might lay hold of him"), ﴿مِنهُ﴾ is explained as referring to the one spoken of in the verse, ﴿بِاليَمِينِ﴾ is explained as "بِالقُوَّةِ والقُدْرَة," meaning "with strength and capability."

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 46:

﴿Then We would have cut off from him the aorta (al-watin).﴾ It is the sinews of the heart (niyat al-qalb), and it is a vein connected to it; when it is severed, its owner dies.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 47:

﴿So there is none among you who could withhold Us from him﴾ (lit. "who could be a barrier against him"). Here "ما" is its noun (ism), and "مِن" is an extra (zaʾida) particle used to emphasize the negation. "مِنكُمْ" is a circumstantial phrase (ḥāl) qualifying "أحَد". ﴿ʿanhu ḥājizīn﴾ means "preventing," and it is the predicate (khabar) of "ما". It is in the plural because "أحَد" in a negative context carries the sense of the plural. The pronoun in "عَنْهُ" refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: there is no one to prevent us from him in terms of punishment.
And indeed it (i.e., the Qur'an)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 49:

﴿And indeed, We know that among you﴾ O people, ﴿are those who deny﴾ the Qur'an ﴿and those who affirm it﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 50:

﴿And indeed it﴾ (i.e., the Qur'an) ﴿is indeed a cause of regret for the disbelievers﴾ when they see the reward of those who affirm it as true and the punishment of those who deny it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 51:

﴿And indeed, it﴾ i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is truly the certain truth﴾ i.e., the true certainty.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 69, verse 52:

﴿So glorify﴾, declare Him free of imperfection, ﴿in the name of﴾ the bāʾ (the preposition bi-) is extra, ﴿your Lord, the Mighty﴾, glory be to Him.
